knowledge_point.title: Calculating a Matrix Product Using the Associative Law

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, recall the associative law

$$
ABC=(AB)C=A(BC).
$$

Notice that $A$ is a $3\times 2$ matrix, $B$ is a $2\times 1$ matrix, and $C$ is a $1\times 3$ matrix. Therefore, 

- multiplying $A$ by $B$, we will obtain a $3\times 1$ matrix, which will require finding $3$ entries, while

- multiplying $B$ by $C$, we will obtain a $2\times 3$ matrix, which will require finding $6$ entries.

So, we find the product $AB$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & 6 \\ 4 & 2 \\ -1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -2\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply $AB$ by $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}ABC & =(AB)C \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ 8 \\ -7\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-1 & 1 & 3\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}3 & -3 & -9 \\ -8 & 8 & 24 \\ 7 & -7 & -21\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

- multiplying $A$ by $B$, we will obtain a $2\times 1$ matrix, which will require finding $2$ entries, while

- multiplying $B$ by $C$, we will obtain a $3\times 2$ matrix, which will require finding $6$ entries.

So, we find the product $AB$ first:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 2\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 8\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we multiply $AB$ by $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}ABC & =(AB)C \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}11 \\ 8\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-1 & 1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-11 & 11 \\ -8 & 8\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}

$$
ABC=(AB)C=A(BC).

Notice that $A$ is a $1\times 2$ matrix, $B$ is a $2\times 1$ matrix, and $C$ is a $1\times 3$ matrix. Therefore, 

- multiplying $A$ by $B$, we will obtain a $1\times 1$ matrix, which will require finding only $1$ entry, while

- multiplying $B$ by $C$, we will obtain a $2\times 3$ matrix, which will require finding $6$ entries.

So, we find the product $AB$ first: 

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =\begin{bmatrix}6 & -2\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 3\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}6\cdot (-1)+(-2)\cdot 3\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-6-6\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-12\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}ABC & =(AB)\,C \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-12\end{bmatrix}\cdot \begin{bmatrix}2 & -4 & 5\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}-24 & 48 & -60\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
